case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.reason: Judgment states 48 persons were arrayed as accused.

accused_gender.reason: Judgment never states the accused's genders; 'Mixed' is not backed by the text.

accused_age.reason: No accused age is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religion is stated for the accused.

accused_caste.reason: No caste is stated for the accused.

accused_occupation.quote: the contractors of the licensed vend
accused_occupation.reason: Respondents are described as contractors of licensed liquor vends; consistent with the value.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victims' genders are not stated; 'Mixed' is not supported by the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Vendor and customers (victims bought liquor from respondents' vends)
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment shows a vendor-customer relationship, with at least one victim knowing the vendor personally, not strangers.

offence_category.correct_value: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.120B; s.300 fourthly)
offence_category.quote: bring their case within the four corners of Section 300 fourthly
offence_category.reason: Convictions were under s.302 and the court applied s.300 fourthly, which is murder, not culpable homicide.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302 r/w s.120B; IPC s.328 r/w s.120B; Punjab Excise Act s.61(1)(a)
statutory_provisions.quote: Section 61(1)(a) of the Punjab Excise Act, 1914
statutory_provisions.reason: Section 34 IPC is not mentioned; the Punjab Excise Act conviction under s.61(1)(a) is omitted.

weapon.correct_value: Spurious liquor adulterated with methyl alcohol (poison)
weapon.reason: No conventional weapon, but the means was poisonous methyl-adulterated liquor, which the value omits.

evidence_type.reason: Medical, witness statements and circumstantial evidence (recovered bottles, conduct) are all relied upon.

confession.reason: No confession by the respondents is mentioned; accused were interrogated leading to recoveries only.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Sale of poisonous liquor and attempt to destroy evidence are both highlighted as aggravating.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are stated in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under IPC s.302 r/w s.120B, s.328 r/w s.120B, and Punjab Excise Act s.61(1)(a)
trial_court_outcome.quote: for the offences under Section 302 IPC read with Section 120B IPC
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under s.302 (murder) and other sections, not culpable homicide.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court allowed the appeal and acquitted the respondents.

final_outcome.quote: judgment of the High Court acquitting the respondents is hereby set aside and that of the trial court convicting the respondents is restored
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court restored the trial court's conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: bring their case within the four corners of Section 300 fourthly
offence_finally_established.reason: Court held the case fell within s.300 fourthly, which is murder, not culpable homicide.

imprisonment_type.quote: directed to undergo imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: The s.302 sentence was life imprisonment, not a fixed term.

imprisonment_years.quote: directed to undergo imprisonment for life
imprisonment_years.reason: The judgment gives life imprisonment for s.302; no 20-year term appears.

fine_rs.quote: also to pay fine ofRs.10,000/- each
fine_rs.reason: Rs.10,000 is the s.302 fine only; other fines under s.328 and the Excise Act are omitted.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts only, without the Supreme Court's outcome (remove reference to the Supreme Court overturning the acquittal)
neutral_facts.quote: The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's acquittal, finding sufficient evidence to connect the respondents to the tragedy.
neutral_facts.reason: Neutral facts reveal the Supreme Court's outcome, which the field must not do.

offence_severity.quote: imprisonment for a term of 5 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- each
offence_severity.reason: Life term with Rs.10,000 fine and 5-year term with Rs.5,000 fine match the judgment; Excise Act sentence omitted but not contradicted.

attempt_completion.reason: Deaths and blindings occurred, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.quote: as many as 44 unfortunate persons who fell prey to it
physical_harm.reason: Judgment records 36 deaths and 44 cases of permanent blindness from methyl alcohol.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Not stated as a count of offences; 48 arrayed as accused, 2 convicted, others acquitted
number_of_offences.reason: Accused counts are accurate, but the judgment does not state a count of offences.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is discussed; compensation is for deaths and blindness, not property.

premeditation_planning.quote: the planned sale of methyl alcohol caused havoc
premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment describes a planned sale and knowledge of consequences, supporting the value.

motive.quote: they were perhaps more interested in making easy money
motive.reason: Greed for quick money is identified as the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Medical evidence, victims' statements and post-offence conduct are accepted as stated.

witness_credibility.quote: there is no reason to disbelieve them
witness_credibility.reason: Court found contemporaneous statements credible and not to be disbelieved.

post_offence_conduct.quote: tried to destroy the evidence in the form of other bottles ... by throwing them away in the river/canal
post_offence_conduct.reason: Destruction of remaining bottles by throwing them in river/canal is accurately recorded.

custody_duration.reason: Custody duration is not stated; respondents were directed to surrender.

trial_duration.reason: Dates for trial judgment, High Court and Supreme Court decisions match the judgment.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the listed appearances.

investigation_status.quote: 48 persons were sent up to stand their trial
investigation_status.reason: FIR, investigation, charge sheeting and completed trial are supported.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Police lapses in investigation; State failed to conduct inquiry into the tragedy
procedural_irregularity.quote: there have been some lapses on the part of the police authorities in not investigating the case with the vigour that was necessitated
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment notes investigative lapses and State administrative failure, so 'None noted' is contradicted.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court acquittal and Supreme Court restoration are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution case on methyl alcohol deaths, victims' statements and destruction of bottles is accurately described.

defence_argument.correct_value: No evidence of consumption from respondents' bottles; no proof of knowledge or conspiracy; charge framing objections under CrPC ss.218/226
defence_argument.quote: there is no proof of the fact that any of the deceased or the persons who lost their vision had actually consumed liquor sold to them
defence_argument.reason: The 'faulty investigation' framing is not the main defence argument; the judgment records other specific defence points.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Section 300 fourthly IPC (murder) and Section 120B IPC; respondents had full knowledge of consequences
legal_principle_applied.quote: bring their case within the four corners of Section 300 fourthly
legal_principle_applied.reason: Value wrongly calls s.300 'culpable homicide not amounting to murder'; the court applied s.300 fourthly, which is murder.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Joseph Kurian Philip Jose v. State of Kerala ... Fakhruddin v. State of MP
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Both cases are cited in the judgment as referred to.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Supreme Court restored trial court's conviction and sentences; respondents directed to surrender; culpability reasons given for conviction
sentencing_rationale.quote: The respondents shall surrender to undergo the sentence inflicted by the trial court.
sentencing_rationale.reason: Court did not impose a new sentence; it restored the trial court's sentence, so the rationale mischaracterises it.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The judgment identifies no mitigating factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: It is this greed and philistinism of the respondents to make quick money
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Greed, exploitation of villagers, knowledge of danger and evidence destruction are all weighed by the court.

other_sentence_order.quote: compensation ofRs.2,00,000/- each to the heirs of36 persons
other_sentence_order.reason: Compensation directions and non-interference after disbursement are accurately described.
